What is WebAssembly and how does it differ from JavaScript?

WebAssembly (Wasm) is a binary instruction format for a stack-based virtual machine. It is a compilation target for languages like C, C++, and Rust.

**Key differences from JavaScript:**
| | WebAssembly | JavaScript |
|-|-|-|
| Speed | Near-native (compiled) | Interpreted/JIT |
| Format | Binary (.wasm) + text (.wat) | Source text |
| Types | Static (i32, i64, f32, f64) | Dynamic |
| Use case | CPU-intensive computation | General web scripting |

**Tools:**
- `wat2wasm` — convert WAT text format to binary
- `wasm2wat` — convert binary to text
- `emscripten` — compile C/C++ to Wasm
- `wasm-pack` — compile Rust to Wasm

```bash
wat2wasm hello.wat -o hello.wasm
```

Wasm runs in browsers, Node.js, and via WASI on servers — enabling portable, sandboxed execution.

How does the WebAssembly Text Format (WAT) work? Show a basic module.

```wat
;; Basic module structure
(module
  ;; Memory (1 page = 64KiB)
  (memory 1)
  (export "memory" (memory 0))

  ;; Global variable (mutable)
  (global $counter (mut i32) (i32.const 0))

  ;; Constant
  (global $PI f64 (f64.const 3.14159265358979))

  ;; Data segment (initialize memory at offset 0)
  (data (i32.const 0) "Hello, World!\n")

  ;; Function: add two i32 integers
  (func $add (export "add") (param $a i32) (param $b i32) (result i32)
    local.get $a   ;; push a onto stack
    local.get $b   ;; push b onto stack
    i32.add        ;; pop two, push sum
  )

  ;; Function with local variables
  (func $sum_to_n (export "sum_to_n") (param $n i32) (result i32)
    (local $result i32)   ;; local variable
    (local $i i32)
    i32.const 0
    local.set $result
    i32.const 0
    local.set $i
    (block $break
      (loop $continue
        local.get $i
        local.get $n
        i32.ge_s
        br_if $break       ;; break if i >= n
        local.get $result
        local.get $i
        i32.add
        local.set $result
        local.get $i
        i32.const 1
        i32.add
        local.set $i
        br $continue       ;; continue loop
      )
    )
    local.get $result
  )
)
```

What are the WebAssembly value types and key instructions?

```wat
;; Value types:
;; i32 — 32-bit integer
;; i64 — 64-bit integer
;; f32 — 32-bit float
;; f64 — 64-bit float
;; v128 — 128-bit SIMD vector (Wasm SIMD extension)

;; Integer constants
i32.const 42
i64.const 9000000000
f32.const 3.14
f64.const 3.14159265358979

;; Integer arithmetic
i32.add; i32.sub; i32.mul
i32.div_s    ;; signed division
i32.div_u    ;; unsigned division
i32.rem_s    ;; signed remainder
i32.and; i32.or; i32.xor
i32.shl      ;; shift left
i32.shr_s    ;; shift right signed
i32.shr_u    ;; shift right unsigned
i32.clz      ;; count leading zeros
i32.popcnt   ;; count set bits

;; Integer comparison
i32.eq; i32.ne
i32.lt_s; i32.lt_u
i32.gt_s; i32.gt_u
i32.eqz      ;; equal to zero

;; Float arithmetic
f64.add; f64.sub; f64.mul; f64.div
f64.sqrt; f64.abs; f64.neg
f64.ceil; f64.floor; f64.trunc
f64.min; f64.max

;; Conversions
i32.wrap_i64         ;; i64 -> i32 (truncate)
i64.extend_i32_s     ;; i32 -> i64 (sign extend)
f64.convert_i32_s    ;; i32 -> f64
i32.trunc_f64_s      ;; f64 -> i32 (truncate)
i32.reinterpret_f32  ;; reinterpret bits

;; select (ternary)
local.get $a
local.get $b
local.get $condition
select            ;; pushes a if condition != 0, else b
```

How do memory operations work in WebAssembly?

```wat
(module
  (memory 1)   ;; 1 page = 64KiB

  (func $memory_ops
    ;; Store i32 at address 0
    i32.const 0      ;; address
    i32.const 42     ;; value
    i32.store        ;; write 4 bytes at address 0

    ;; Load i32 from address 0
    i32.const 0
    i32.load         ;; => 42

    ;; Store/load bytes
    i32.const 100
    i32.const 255
    i32.store8       ;; write 1 byte

    i32.const 100
    i32.load8_u      ;; zero-extended load
    i32.load8_s      ;; sign-extended load

    ;; 16-bit operations
    i32.const 200
    i32.const 1000
    i32.store16
    i32.const 200
    i32.load16_u

    ;; With alignment hint (2^n)
    i32.const 0
    i32.load align=4
  )

  ;; Grow memory (returns old size in pages, or -1 on failure)
  (func $grow (param $pages i32) (result i32)
    local.get $pages
    memory.grow
  )

  ;; Current size in pages
  (func $size (result i32)
    memory.size
  )
)
```

How does WASI (WebAssembly System Interface) work?

```wat
;; WASI — system interface for running Wasm outside browser
(module
  ;; Import WASI functions
  (import "wasi_snapshot_preview1" "fd_write"
    (func $fd_write (param i32 i32 i32 i32) (result i32)))

  (memory 1)
  (export "memory" (memory 0))

  ;; "Hello, WASI!\n" stored at offset 8
  (data (i32.const 8) "Hello, WASI!\n")

  (func $main (export "_start")
    ;; iovec: {ptr=8, len=13}
    (i32.store (i32.const 0) (i32.const 8))   ;; buf ptr
    (i32.store (i32.const 4) (i32.const 13))  ;; buf len

    ;; fd_write(stdout=1, iovec_ptr=0, count=1, nwritten_ptr=20)
    (call $fd_write
      (i32.const 1)   ;; stdout
      (i32.const 0)   ;; iovec pointer
      (i32.const 1)   ;; 1 iovec
      (i32.const 20)  ;; nwritten output
    )
    drop
  )
)
```

```bash
# Compile with WASI
emcc hello.c -o hello.wasm -s STANDALONE_WASM --target=wasm32-wasi

# Run with wasmtime (WASI runtime)
wasmtime hello.wasm

# Run with Node.js WASI
node --experimental-wasi-unstable-preview1 run.mjs
```

WASI provides system calls (file I/O, sockets, clock, random) through a standard interface, making Wasm portable across operating systems without a browser.
